newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended the Christmas week slightly firmer against the dollar, propped up by exporter sales of the U.S. unit in quiet dealings, dealers said on Friday.
They said the local unit was expected to continue its firmer trend next week as the stream of export business, mainly from mining houses, continued.
"We saw some exporters for most of the day. There were even some fairly decent volumes," one trader said.
Another trader said a handful of importers, usually buyers of dollars, were also seen offloading small volumes of dollars.
"We have also seen some normal importers selling dollars -- either because they are in surplus or because they are uncovering their positions a bit."
The rand ended the day at 4.6800/6850 on the dollar from 4.6865/6915 on Tuesday.
Against the crosses, the rand was weaker against sterling at 7.8850/8981 from 7.8396/8526 against sterling and a touch firmer on the German mark at 0.3322/3327 from 0.3313/3318.
The rand spent most of the day hovering in a tight 4.6800-4.6820 range, with further gains capped by importer activity and some demand for dollars from offshore at the bottom end of the band.
"There was some importer demand around the 4.68 level...there was also shortly before lunch some dollar demand from a fund manager based in London," a dealer said.

Traders said business volumes were expected to return to normal only from January 6 with trading next week again interrupted by holidays. The currency market is seen closing at 1000 GMT on Tuesday ahead of the New Year's Day holiday on Wednesday.
The bond market was closed on Friday leaving the key benchmark long bond stuck at Tuesday's closing level of 16.14 percent. The market will resume trading on Monday.
On the money market three-month NCD rates were steady at 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at a year high of 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
The money market shortage rose to 10.790 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.786 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said on Friday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners sold a net 25.38 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after buying 2.19 million on Friday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 793.79 million rand on Monday from 2.43 billion rand on Friday.
Bond figures for Tuesday were not available as the Exchange was closed on Friday.
